speech: There is no recognised health-based guidance value, such as an Acceptable Daily Intake, for caffeine. However, a report published by a Food Standards Australia New Zealand Expert Working Group concludes: firstly, that there are reports of increased anxiety levels at caffeine doses of 95 milligrams in children and doses of 210 milligrams in adults; secondly, that caffeine has been reported to reduce the ability to sleep at doses of 100 milligrams at bedtime; thirdly, it is concluded that caffeine at doses typically consumed in the diet may lead to withdrawal effects and some physical dependence in adults.
